headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: ctx can read filesystem/MCP context while next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and multi-LLM API access.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and uses mcp/stdio, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if content from one is fed into the other through shared files or MCP, though no direct shared channel is documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ctx ingests next-ai-draw-io-generated text from a shared file or MCP message, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF next-ai-draw-io renders or reuses ctx output as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces.
Disable automatic ingestion of generated text as instructions.
Add provenance tags to files passed between agents.
Review any MCP bridge before enabling it.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches filesystem, audit/runtime logs, graph data, and MCP servers; next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, images, diagrams, and requests broad network egress to multiple model APIs. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from ctx into next-ai-draw-io and then to third-party inference endpoints. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from profiles alone, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same directory, files touched by ctx can be opened by next-ai-draw-io.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends document contents to external model APIs, shared files may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent.
Remove sensitive files from the shared workspace.
Prefer local-only models for next-ai-draw-io.
Restrict outbound network access during shared runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and ctx writes to filesystem while next-ai-draw-io processes files and can use MCP plus broad network egress. Overlapping mutable access can cause races or overwrites if they operate on the same diagrams or workspace. No locking is documented, so the conflict is real but not clearly high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory, file clobbering or stale reads can occur.
IF both instances modify the same diagram or metadata concurrently, last-writer-wins conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate output directory.
Serialize writes to shared files.
Use git branches or per-agent copies.
Pause one agent before the other edits the same artifact.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a context-management agent that observes tool events, and next-ai-draw-io performs AI-assisted visualization from natural-language commands. If ctx output is forwarded into next-ai-draw-io without verification, errors or hallucinated facts can be rendered into diagrams or acted on. The profiles do not show strong verification gates, so the cascade is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF ctx-generated summaries are used as authoritative input to next-ai-draw-io, errors can propagate into diagrams.
IF next-ai-draw-io auto-applies natural-language instructions derived from ctx output, downstream mistakes can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review before diagram generation.
Compare outputs against source files.
Use a checklist for any ctx-to-diagram handoff.
Keep raw source artifacts alongside generated diagrams.
requires-engineering: add verification and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, while next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and can send content to multiple external AI providers. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if the same regulated data class enters both systems. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs and then forwarded to next-ai-draw-io, retention obligations may diverge.
IF next-ai-draw-io transmits EU or sensitive data to external APIs, residency or DPA requirements may be implicated.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Redact logs before handoff.
Use a local-only model path.
Review retention settings for both tools.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
